doc: Each case is a quality-card manifest (cards array, wrapped in a fast-mlx-quality-card-v1 envelope by each test) plus the launch identity (repo, revision, hostHardwareClass; null means absent / unrecognized host). expect is the ENGINE outcome: "none" | {"card": id} | {"ambiguous": {"repo": [ids], "pin": [ids]}} (id lists sorted). The Swift test loads the cards through the engine's own manifest decoder (QualityCardStore.loadManifestDetailed) and calls QualityCardStore.resolve(repo:revision:hostHardwareClass:in:); the Python test runs fastmlx_launch.resolve_card. SCOPE HELD FIXED: Python's engine_build_commit tiebreak and residency argument have no Swift counterpart in resolve, so the Python side runs every case with residency="resident" and engine_build_commit=None, and the host class is injected on both sides; the table says nothing about those two inputs. knownPythonDivergence {pythonOutcome, reason}, when present, is a documented difference in the ONLY tolerated direction: Python refuses (LaunchRefusal exit 3) where the engine picks a card. Python returning a card where the engine returns none, ambiguous or a different card is never tolerated, and the Python test rejects any divergence entry that claims otherwise. Python's ambiguous outcome is also a refusal (exit 3, naming the sorted repo and pin ids). Repos, card ids and revisions are synthetic. Expectations are hand-authored from the documented rule in QualityAdmission.swift select/resolve; where the engine disagreed with a guess the why says engine-observed.

cases.why: A repo match with no revision: the single repo card.
No card names this repo and no revision: none.
Neither repo nor revision: nothing to match, none.
A full-hex revision that is not any card's pin leaves the pin pool empty, so the repo card resolves without ambiguity.
A card whose repo is null (pin-only card) is never matched by a repo lookup.
A pin-only card (repo null) whose 8-hex hfPin is a prefix of the full revision resolves by pin.
A repo that names no card does not block a pin match: the pin pool becomes the candidates.
A pin-only card cannot match without a revision.
A 40-hex hfPin equal to the revision is a prefix of it (prefix includes equality).
A 12-hex hfPin is a longer-than-minimum prefix; matches by prefix, not equality.
A 7-hex hfPin is below the 8-hex minimum: never matches, though it is a true prefix.
An 8-hex hfPin that is not a prefix of the revision does not match.
An 8-char hfPin containing a non-hex character is not a usable pin.
An hfPin longer than the revision cannot be its prefix.
Pin comparison is case-insensitive: an uppercase 8-hex pin matches a lowercase revision.
An uppercase 40-hex revision still matches a lowercase pin.
A 39-hex revision is not a full sha: the pin pool is empty.
A 41-hex revision is not a full sha: the pin pool is empty.
A 40-char revision containing a non-hex character is not a full sha.
A 39-hex revision empties the pin pool, so a pin-only sibling cannot cause ambiguity against the repo card.
One card matched both by repo and by pin: the same identity on both sides is not ambiguous.
Two hardware siblings matched by both repo and pin form the same identity set on both sides, so the shared selection rule runs (lowest id with no host).
The repo names card-a and the pin names card-b (a pin-only card): ambiguous, never a silent preference.
Ambiguous id lists are sorted ids: manifest order is c-then-a for the repo side.
The repo pool is {card-a} and the pin pool is {card-a, card-b}: different identity sets, ambiguous.
A PASS repo card and a NO_GO pin-only card published under one id: the id sets match but the identities differ, so it is still ambiguous (duplicate-id guard).
The pin-only card is expert-stream (filtered before ambiguity), so the repo card resolves.
No config object at all means measured resident: eligible.
A config object with no residency key means resident: eligible.
config.residency null means resident: eligible.
config.residency 'resident': eligible.
A lone expert-stream card never gates a resident launch: none.
A lone card with an unrecognized residency string never matches a resident launch: none.
A NO_GO expert-stream card is invisible; the resident PASS sibling resolves (engine behavior: filtered cards leave the pool even when NO_GO).
A NO_GO card with an unrecognized residency is invisible too: the resident PASS card resolves. Treating unknown as resident would let the NO_GO narrow the pool.
An empty-string residency is not null and not 'resident': unrecognized, never matches.
Residency matching is exact: 'Resident' is unrecognized, never matches.
Host on the PASS card's class: hardwareClass is a tiebreak within the NO_GO pool, never a filter, so the NO_GO card still resolves (fail-closed).
Host on the NO_GO card's class: the NO_GO card.
Host on neither class: the NO_GO pool's only member, even though the PASS card has the lowest id.
Unrecognized host: the NO_GO pool's only member.
Manifest order must never decide: same pair reversed.
A NO_GO beats an EXACT sibling even with a host match on the EXACT card.
The NO_GO narrowing applies equally to a pin-derived pool.
Two NO_GO siblings and a PASS: the pool is the two NO_GO cards; the PASS host match is excluded and the lowest NO_GO id wins.
Two NO_GO siblings and a PASS: a unique host match inside the NO_GO pool beats the lowest NO_GO id.
Two PASS siblings; the host matches the higher-id one uniquely, so it wins over the lowest id.
Host matches the lower-id sibling uniquely.
Host matches neither sibling: lowest id, not a refusal and not a filter.
Unrecognized host: lowest id.
The host matches two cards (not unique), so the host does not narrow and the lowest id of the whole tie pool wins (a@hw1), not the lowest id among the host matches (b@hw2).
All siblings share the host's class: no unique match, lowest id.
Cards with no recorded hardwareClass never host-match: lowest id.
One card records the host's class and a sibling records none: the unique host match wins over the lowest id.
The host tiebreak runs the same over a pin-derived pool.
Three PASS siblings listed c, a, b with no host: the lowest id regardless of manifest order.
Two NO_GO hardware siblings, unrecognized host (the shipped multi-hardware shape): lowest id. Python used to refuse here; the 2026-09-26 DECISION made it take the same-verdict lowest id.
Two NO_GO siblings, host on neither: lowest id.
UNMEASURED siblings share one verdict: lowest id.
Two cards, one filtered by residency: a single survivor is returned without any tiebreak.
Two structurally different cards share one id (differ only in hardwareClass). Engine: picks by id (either is that id). Python refuses because the lowest id is not unique.

knownPythonDivergence.reason: the lowest id is shared by two structurally different cards; Python refuses (exit 3) where the engine's min-by-id picks one

cases.why: Same shared id, but the host uniquely matches one of them: both sides resolve it.
PASS and EXACT siblings, no NO_GO, no host: the engine picks the lowest id; Python refuses because an arbitrary pick would change the reported verdict.

knownPythonDivergence.reason: mixed non-NO_GO verdicts (PASS and EXACT) with no unique host match: Python refuses (exit 3) rather than pick by lowest id

cases.why: Same pair, host on neither class: still no unique host match, so the same divergence.

knownPythonDivergence.reason: mixed non-NO_GO verdicts with host on neither class: Python refuses (exit 3)

cases.why: A unique host match settles it before the verdict check: both sides pick the EXACT card.
A unique host match on the PASS card: both sides pick PASS.
PASS and REFERENCE siblings: same mixed-verdict divergence.

knownPythonDivergence.reason: mixed non-NO_GO verdicts (REFERENCE and PASS) with no unique host match: Python refuses (exit 3)

cases.why: PASS and UNMEASURED siblings: same mixed-verdict divergence.

knownPythonDivergence.reason: mixed non-NO_GO verdicts (UNMEASURED and PASS) with no unique host match: Python refuses (exit 3)

cases.why: A lone card with an unrecognized verdict still resolves (the engine reads it as UNMEASURED; the card is returned, not dropped).
The recognized NO_GO sibling narrows the pool; a lowercase 'no_go' card is not NO_GO and is excluded from it.
An unrecognized verdict beside a PASS: the engine sees UNMEASURED and PASS siblings and picks the lowest id; Python sees two different raw verdict strings and refuses.

knownPythonDivergence.reason: an unrecognized raw verdict string differs from PASS: Python refuses (exit 3) where the engine picks the lowest id

cases.why: Two distinct unrecognized verdict strings both decode to UNMEASURED in the engine (lowest id); Python counts them as different verdicts and refuses.

knownPythonDivergence.reason: two distinct unrecognized verdict strings: Python refuses (exit 3) where the engine reads both as UNMEASURED and picks the lowest id

cases.why: Two cards with the same unrecognized verdict string form one same-verdict pool in both implementations: lowest id.
